h2: Pool Repair Sanur – Leaks, Tiles & Ageing Pipework
intro: Many villas around Sanur are fifteen to twenty years old, and their pools carry that age in brittle PVC joints, lifting mosaic, and slow leaks nobody can pin down. Pool Repair Sanur jobs here almost always trace back to two things: prolonged UV exposure on original fittings and salt-laden air drifting in from the beach. I look at the whole system first, then tell you what genuinely needs attention before anything else.

sections.h3: Why Sanur Pools Age Faster Than You'd Expect
sections.text: In Sindhu, Semawang and Mertasari the sea breeze reaches your pool equipment within minutes of the shoreline. Taps corrode, pump motor housings pit, and stainless hinges seize long before they should add to the wear. Add brackish well water common near the coast, and filters clog while heaters scale up faster than PDAM-fed systems inland. The result is a pool that looks fine on the surface but hides failing joints under the waterline.

sections.h3: What I Actually Fix Around Here
sections.text: The most common call-outs are a pool losing half a centimetre of water overnight with no visible source, mosaic tiles popping up after a hot spell, grout crumbling along the coping edge, and a weeping joint where two PVC pipes meet. For pipework past its prime, swapping out the affected run is usually cleaner and more durable than epoxy-patching a brittle fitting. I'll walk you through which approach makes sense for your specific setup before any work starts.

sections.h3: Sending Me Photos Before I Visit
sections.text: You don't need a video essay — a couple of clear photos of the problem spot, the pool's approximate size, and one line about when you first noticed it gives me enough to work from. For leaks, note whether the drop accelerates in midday heat or creeps steadily overnight; that distinction saves a visit. Send whatever you have over WhatsApp and I'll reply with a practical next step plus a quote once I can see the job properly.

sections.h3: Small Habits That Save Bigger Repairs
sections.text: A quick monthly wipe-down of pump seals and valve handles stops salt crystals grinding into threads — particularly useful if your villa is nearer the shoreline in Semawang or Batujimbar. Rinsing the filter twice weekly through the dry season keeps brackish sediment from baking onto the media. And if you notice a new tick or faint vibration around the skimmer box, ping me on WhatsApp early; catching a loosening joint before it splits saves far more than replacing a burst pipe later.

faq.q: Do I need to replace all the pipework, or can one section be swapped?
faq.a: Usually just the affected run. Original PVC that has gone chalky-brittle won't hold a patch long-term, but the rest of the system may still have years left. I check the surrounding joints before recommending anything.

faq.q: Is the salt air really making my pool equipment fail sooner?
faq.a: In the beach-side pockets like Sindhu and Mertasari, yes — corrosion on taps, hinges and motor housings runs noticeably faster than inland. A light protective wipe after heavy rain helps, though it won't stop the process entirely.

faq.q: My water level drops slowly but I see no drip anywhere. What could it be?
faq.a: It's often a hairline crack in a buried fitting or a weeping joint under the coping that only shows at certain water levels. Send a photo of the area plus your daily drop estimate on WhatsApp and I'll suggest where to look first.
